rootCause: A deployed task definition revision enabled the leaky read path, so each patient vital request acquired a database session that was never returned and connections grew steadily until the pool was exhausted. Flat request volume ruled out a traffic surge, healthy RDS resources ruled out instance saturation, and the unrelated LOG_LEVEL-only deployment was excluded because it did not align with failure onset.

competingCauseJudgments.rationale: Request volume remained flat through the incident.
RDS CPU and free storage remained healthy.
The LOG_LEVEL-only revision did not align with failure onset.

remediation.summary: Release the leaked connections by redeploying the Healthcare service, then roll the task definition back to the revision whose session pool behaviour was intact.

executionSteps.intent: Return the service to the last healthy task definition.
executionSteps.action: Redeploy the Healthcare service with the previously healthy task definition revision.
executionSteps.successCriteria: Database connections stabilize and vital ingest failures return to zero.

safeguards.preconditions: Confirm the deployed revision enables the leak flag and that the previous revision did not.
safeguards.approval: Require the service owner to approve the redeploy and the revision rollback.
safeguards.rollback: Redeploy the current revision if vital ingest does not recover after the rollback.
safeguards.verification: Verify that DatabaseConnections stops climbing and VitalIngestFailures returns to zero while ingest attempts stay flat.
